subject: Renewal + Capacity: Proposal to move from 8 → 16 GPUs (monthly commit update)
messages:
From: Sophie Barnes <sophie@acmeapp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal coming up — exploring doubling reserved GPUs

Hi Priya,

Our annual contract with Redwood is up for renewal on May 1. Over the last quarter our inference traffic has increased ~2.6x and we’re regularly hitting contention on the 8-GPU reserved pool during peak windows. We’re planning to launch a paid feature in June that will further increase sustained token volume.

We’d like to explore upgrading to 16 GPUs for our Dedicated pool at renewal and update the monthly commit accordingly. Key asks from our side:
- A predictable monthly commit and cost schedule for 16 GPUs (ideally with a phased activation window)
- Throughput guarantees (99th percentile latency SLO during business hours) or clear fallback/credits language
- A short ops playbook for staged activation so the migration doesn’t disrupt jobs

Can your team put together an amendment + ops/activation plan? Procurement and engineering leads are looped on cc.

Thanks,
Sophie Barnes
Head of Platform
Acme App

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and the usage snapshot, that helps a lot. We’re glad to hear the product launch is going well.

Quick response: yes, we can support an upgrade from 8 → 16 GPUs at renewal with a phased activation and explicit throughput guardrails. I’ll summarize the high-level proposal below and attach the draft amendment and a staged activation runbook.

High-level proposal (details in attached):
- Term: 12 months, starting at renewal effective date (May 1)
- Monthly commit: updated to reflect 16-GPU sustained capacity (line-item + per-token overage metric)
- Activation plan: 2-week staggered activation (8→12→16) with smoke tests and rollback gates
- SLA/credits: 99th p50 latency guard (business hours PST), with credit thresholds if we miss sustained throughput target; automatic fallback to compatible model variant when capacity constrained
- Onboarding: one scheduled activation window with Redwood ops support + runbook access

I’ve attached the amendment (redwood_dedicated_8to16_amendment_v2.pdf) and a draft SOW/activation checklist (sow-acme-16gpu.xlsx). Internal: I’ve CC’d Sean (pricing lead) and Marissa (customer ops) to sign off on commercials and the operational plan.

Next steps: I’ll sync with Sean and Marissa to finalize numbers and get a DocuSign ready for procurement. Are there any internal blackout dates in May for the product launch?

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Renewal commercials — initial pricing thoughts

Team — quick internal note before I loop back to Sophie:
- Baseline: convert Acme’s current 8-GPU reserved price to an equivalent 16-GPU commit with a volume discount (we should push for 20% uplift vs list per-GPU, given 2x capacity).
- Phased activation discount: offer a 6-week reduced-rate ramp (50% of incremental GPUs billed) during the staggered activation to reduce migration risk for the customer.
- SLA/credits: agree to an operational SLA for business hours (PST 08:00–18:00), credits up to 10% of monthly commit if sustained throughput falls below targets 2 months in a row. Keep fallback and model-variant clause to avoid unbounded exposure.
- Add a one-time onboarding credit to offset the migration ops time (single invoice line).

Karthik — can you confirm the throughput guard thresholds (tokens/sec per GPU) we should promise for their current model family? Also, we need an explicit ops checklist for the smoke tests.

—Sean
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal commercials — throughput and ops checklist

Sean / team — quick technical confirmations:
- Throughput: for Acme’s primary model family (redwood-1-large), we can guarantee sustained throughput at 0.9x of theoretical single-GPU throughput when using continuous batching + prefix cache, which maps to ~1.8M tokens/hour per GPU under typical request distributions. For a 16-GPU pool that gives ~28.8M tokens/hour sustained across business hours.
- Ramp/rollback tests: recommend three smoke tests during the 2-week activation: 1) prefix-caching warmup (48h), 2) ramp to 75% predicted QPS (4h), 3) sustained 6h run at 95% with monitoring checks. If any test breaches error or latency thresholds, rollback to previous step.
- Ops handoff: provide playbook, runbook, and a daily 30-minute check-in for the first 5 business days.

I’ll add these items into the SOW spreadsheet and mark the guard thresholds.

—Karthik
